ai.title: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Donation and New AI Infrastructure
ai.brief: Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon , the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell , an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate , an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox.

sec.title: AI company Fireworks says hackers stole data, billing info during October breaches
sec.brief: AI infrastructure company Fireworks said cybercriminals stole billing information and AI-specific data during two breaches last month. Fireworks published an updated notice on Monday saying it hired Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 to investigate a data breach it initially discovered on October 6 . The San Mateo-based company was founded in 2022 and has more than 10,000 customers, offering an array of AI systems and tools to companies. Investigators found that a well-known, financially motivated cybercriminal group launched the attack and stole account and billing information as well as secrets — confidential digital pieces of information that grant access to human users or apps and allow them to communicate or perform actions. Fireworks said the incident affected a “limited number of customer accounts” — all of whom were notified of the attack.
